summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of atrial fibrillation and post-herpetic neuralgia was admitted with pain, swelling, and pus drainage at her left femoral dialysis catheter site. She was diagnosed with MRSA catheter-related bacteremia. The infected catheter was removed, and she was treated with intravenous vancomycin. A new tunneled catheter was placed in the right femoral vein, but imaging revealed it had crossed a previously undiagnosed atrial septal defect into the left atrium, with a small thrombus noted on the tip. The clot resolved with 48 hours of heparin, and the catheter was replaced with a shorter one. She developed C. difficile colitis, likely triggered by initial antibiotics, and was treated with oral metronidazole. Antiretroviral therapy was restarted with abacavir, emtricitabine, atazanavir, and ritonavir. She improved clinically, completed a course of antibiotics, and was discharged home with plans to continue vancomycin with dialysis and complete her metronidazole and HIV regimens.
